You are implementing PHASE 1 of the true L3 fused megakernel in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (branch claude/h100-audit-maximal): replace the SURROGATE model stage with the REAL transformer-decoder forward+backward inside the existing persistent megakernel substrate, so that (decoder × adamw) runs as ONE persistent kernel per training step — real model math, real optimizer math, zero intermediate kernel launches. The owner explicitly rejected CUDA graphs; this is the chosen path. A true persistent megakernel: weights/state resident, stages separated only by in-kernel grid barriers.

CONTEXT (verified, trust this):
- The surrogate: csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages.cuh implements acts=GELU(param+input), grad=acts·GELU'(param) — placeholder math. The race input is int64/int32 token indices (decoder x shape [B≈4191, 4-ish] in [0,98]) but the megakernel ABI takes const float* input — ABI must gain a token path.
- Substrate that works: csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh (PersistentContext, grid barrier, task loop), csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh (launch config: gridDim=co-resident CTAs, 256 threads/CTA, launch_fused_megakernel<Model,Opt,Tier>), opt_components.cuh (apply_optimizer<> tails with FusedScalars — recently un-frozen, includes canonical csrc/algorithms/*.h math), megakernel_codegen.py emits the 33 cells + dispatch tables, csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp fused_step (recently widened: full scalar set + opt_only selector).
- The real decoder (grokking_race_v2.py build_model / the decoder class ~line 340-430): embed tokens (vocab 99 → d=128) + learned positional, N=2 transformer layers (pre-LN or post-LN — READ THE PYTHON to match exactly: layernorms, 4-head self-attention d_head=32, causal mask?, MLP dim_ff (read it), residuals), final LN(?), head projecting to 99 logits, cross-entropy on the LAST token position (READ the loss: F.cross_entropy(m(tx), ty) — check what m() returns: logits for the answer position). You MUST transcribe the exact eager architecture — read the Python model class line by line, including dropout (probably 0/absent), activation (GELU/ReLU), bias usage, and the exact loss reduction (mean over batch).
- Race batch: full-batch B≈4191, seq 4-5 tokens (p=97 task "a op b ="), fixed shapes per run. fp32 master weights; the race now defaults to bf16 autocast for eager — for the megakernel do fp32 compute first (correctness baseline); bf16 compute is a follow-up flag.
- Validation harness pattern: tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py (agent-built, CPU plumbing tests + GPU parity runner). Extend it.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
1. New real decoder stages in csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages.cuh (replace/augment the surrogate behind ModelId::TransformerDecoder + a compile-time REAL_MODEL flag or new tier so the surrogate stays compilable for the other cells until their phases land): forward (embed+pos → L×[LN, MHA(4 heads, dhead 32, seq≤8 — attention scores can live in registers/smem per CTA), residual, LN, MLP, residual] → final LN → head → softmax+CE loss on answer position) and backward (full chain to ALL weight grads + embedding grads). Batch-sliced persistence: each CTA owns a contiguous batch slice, computes its slice's fwd+bwd entirely locally (activations in smem where they fit, else registers/local), accumulates per-CTA weight-grad partials; then ONE grid barrier; then a reduction stage (sum partials across CTAs — pre-allocated workspace, deterministic tree or atomicAdd — prefer deterministic for reproducibility); then the existing apply_optimizer<> tail consumes the reduced grads in-place. Loss (scalar, for logging) written to a device float.
2. ABI: extend fused_step (csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp — you own it now; agent A's widened version is in the tree, keep its scalars) with the token input path: const int32 tokens [B, S], targets [B], plus B/S/vocab/d dims + a workspace tensor (weight-grad partials + loss). Python side: grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py fused_optimizer_step / a new fused_train_step(model_params_flat, tokens, targets, state, scalars...) and the _try_fused_step wiring in grokking_race_v2.py for the decoder×adamw cell (whitelist-gated as before; this REPLACES the eager fwd+bwd+step for that cell when enabled — the loop must use the kernel's returned loss for logging and skip its own forward/backward; eval_every evaluation stays eager/unchanged).
3. Weight layout: the megakernel sees params as ONE flat float buffer + sizes/offsets. Generate the offsets from the eager model's named_parameters() order — write the exact mapping in ONE place (Python) and mirror it in a C++ header with static asserts on counts; a mismatch must fail loudly at dispatch, not corrupt.
4. Determinism: fixed reduction order (no float atomics in the weight-grad reduce if avoidable).
5. Validation (extend tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py): (a) single-step parity — same init/batch: loss matches eager fp32 within 1e-5 rel, every weight grad within 1e-4 rel (dump max-rel-err per tensor), params after 1 step within 1e-5; (b) 200-step trajectory: loss curve agreement + final params 1e-3 rel; (c) 3-seed grok smoke on decoder×adamw (uses race budget). DO NOT RUN GPU work — tuning owns the GPU; deliver source + the runbook update (append a PHASE-1 section to BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md).
6. Codegen: if the cells' host entries need a new signature for the token path, update megakernel_codegen.py and regenerate ALL cells/tables in the same pass (git diff must stay generator-consistent). Cells other than decoder keep the surrogate path compiling (loud readiness gating already exists in dispatch.py — extend _FUSED_READY semantics with a tier marker so decoder×adamw can be marked L3-REAL while others stay L1/per-op).
7. Honesty rails: no placeholder math anywhere on the new path; if a piece must be deferred (e.g. bf16 compute), it is a flag defaulting to the working fp32 path with a loud comment, never a silent stub. Comment WHY at every design point. All Python AST-checked; C++ braces balanced (you cannot compile — be rigorous by reading).

File ownership: you own csrc/fused/**, csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp, grokking_optimizers/{dispatch.py,megakernel_codegen.py,megakernel_engine.py}, tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py, BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md, and the _try_fused_step block in grokking_race_v2.py (touch ONLY that function + the decoder/adamw call site in it; another agent recently edited other parts of that file — re-read before editing). Do NOT touch csrc/algorithms/*.h, kernels/sm_90/*_sm90.cuh, bindings.cpp, setup.py, build.sh, tuning/ (other agents' territory).

Report when done: the exact architecture you transcribed (layer by layer, citing the Python lines), the stage/barrier layout, smem budget per CTA, the weight-layout mapping, ABI changes, what's validated by which test, and the runbook delta.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	#pragma once
2	// csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh
3	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4	// Stage 6 — sm_90 L3 persistent-megakernel internals (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14).
5	//
6	// This header is the **uniform scheduler + barrier substrate** that every
7	// generated L3 megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu) composes on top of the §3.4
8	// warp-specialization primitives (csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh).
9	// It defines ONLY the cross-CTA coordination machinery; the per-(model,
10	// optimizer) compute stages live in the generated TUs.
11	//
12	// The four pieces, all sm_90-real (compile-verified via
13	// scripts/compile_to_object.sh) and degrading to a correct fallback on older
14	// arches so the codegen matrix still builds:
15	//
16	//   §1.1  TaskQueue        — a single global atomic work counter that every
17	//                            persistent CTA pulls parameter-tensor indices
18	//                            from (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern).
19	//   §1.2  work-stealing     — there is NO static partition: an idle CTA simply
20	//                            keeps calling TaskQueue::next(), so a CTA that
21	//                            finishes its tensor early steals the next one.
22	//                            (atomicAdd on the shared counter IS the steal.)
23	//   §1.3  sm_id()           — reads %smid so the host can pin one persistent
24	//                            CTA per SM and keep that SM's optimizer-state
25	//                            slice L2-warm across the step.
26	//   §1.4  GridBarrier       — a hand-built arrive/wait grid barrier from two
27	//                            global atomics + a sense-reversing generation
28	//                            counter. Reusable, needs NO cooperative launch
29	//                            (so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap).
30	//
31	// §1.14 fences: acquire/release are placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY — exactly
32	// one __threadfence() before the arrival publish and one acquire load after
33	// the release wait at the barrier, and one fence at the task hand-off. No loose
34	// fences (a loose fence here is both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun).
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	
37	#include "csrc/common/platform.h"
38	#include "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh"
39	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
40	
41	namespace sg { namespace fused {
42	
43	// =========================================================================
44	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
45	//
46	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
47	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
48	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
49	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
50	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
51	// =========================================================================
52	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
53	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
54	    unsigned id;
55	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
56	    return id;
57	#else
58	    return 0u;
59	#endif
60	}
61	
62	// =========================================================================
63	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
64	//
65	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
66	//  Every CTA runs:
67	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
68	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
69	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
70	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
71	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
72	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
73	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
74	//
75	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
76	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
77	// =========================================================================
78	struct TaskQueue {
79	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
80	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
81	
82	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
83	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
84	
85	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
86	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
87	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
88	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
89	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
90	    }
91	
92	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
93	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
94	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
96	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
97	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
98	        }
99	        __syncthreads();
100	        int t = *smem_slot;
101	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
102	        return t;
103	    }
104	};
105	
106	// =========================================================================
107	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
108	//
109	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
110	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
111	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
112	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
113	//
114	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
115	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
116	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
117	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
118	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
119	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
120	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
121	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
122	//
123	//  Fences (§1.14):
124	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
125	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
126	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
127	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
128	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
129	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
130	//
131	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
132	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
133	// =========================================================================
134	struct GridBarrier {
135	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
136	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
137	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
138	
139	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
140	                                            unsigned* generation,
141	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
142	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
143	
144	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
145	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
146	        __syncthreads();
147	
148	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
149	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
150	            unsigned my_gen =
151	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
152	
153	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
154	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
155	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
156	            __threadfence();
157	
158	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
159	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
160	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
161	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
162	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
163	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
164	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
165	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
166	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
167	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
168	                __threadfence();
169	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
170	            } else {
171	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
172	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
173	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
174	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
175	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
176	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
177	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
178	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
179	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
180	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
181	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
182	                       == my_gen) {
183	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
184	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
185	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
186	#endif
187	                }
188	            }
189	
190	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
191	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
192	            __threadfence();
193	        }
194	
195	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
196	        __syncthreads();
197	    }
198	
199	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
200	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
201	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
202	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
203	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
204	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
205	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
206	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
207	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
208	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
209	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
210	        __syncthreads();
211	
212	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
213	            unsigned my_gen =
214	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
215	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
216	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
217	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
218	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
219	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
220	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
221	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
222	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
223	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
224	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
225	                __threadfence();
226	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
227	            } else {
228	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
229	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
230	                       == my_gen) {
231	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
232	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
233	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
234	#endif
235	                }
236	            }
237	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
238	        }
239	
240	        __syncthreads();
241	    }
242	};
243	
244	// =========================================================================
245	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
246	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
247	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
248	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
249	// =========================================================================
250	struct PersistentContext {
251	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
252	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
253	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
254	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
255	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
256	
257	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
258	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
259	    }
260	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
261	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
262	    }
263	};
264	
265	}} // namespace sg::fused

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh — REAL per-optimizer device-function
5	// composition library for the sm_90 fused L3 megakernel (Phase 3 Stage 5).
6	//
7	// THIS REPLACES THE FALSE POSITIVE. The previous fused path (megakernel_demo.cu
8	// :opt_update<Opt>) implemented only 4 optimizers (AdamW/Lion/Muon/SuperGrok15)
9	// with TOY math, and the codegen mapped the other 7 to the AdamW tail — i.e.
10	// `mega_*_prodigy.cu` actually ran AdamW. That is the breadth-faking this stage
11	// eliminates.
12	//
13	// Here every one of the 11 optimizers calls its OWN, REAL per-element update
14	// function from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (the canonical optimizer component —
15	// the same device functions the per-op launchers compile). No fallback, no
16	// templating one optimizer from another, no toy substitute. Each optimizer's
17	// genuine state buffers are plumbed through FusedOptState.
18	//
19	// SCOPE / HONESTY (the fused TAIL vs the outer loop):
20	//   The L3 megakernel fuses the per-element optimizer TAIL after fwd+bwd. The
21	//   multi-phase OUTER parts that are not per-element — Muon's Newton–Schulz
22	//   orthogonalization, Prodigy's global d reduction, LookSAM's perturb/restore
23	//   ascent, SG11/SG15's cosine-gate reduction, and SG2's CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net
24	//   — run as their own launch(es) and hand this tail the precomputed result
25	//   (orth direction, d factor, sam_dir, reduced gate, smart-grad). This mirrors
26	//   the real per-op pipelines exactly; the tail math below IS the real apply.
27	// ============================================================================
28	
29	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
30	#include <cstdint>
31	
32	// The 11 canonical optimizer components (real per-element device functions).
33	#include "csrc/algorithms/adamw.h"
34	#include "csrc/algorithms/lion.h"
35	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokfast.h"
36	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h"
37	#include "csrc/algorithms/looksam.h"
38	#include "csrc/algorithms/prodigy.h"
39	#include "csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h"
40	#include "csrc/algorithms/muon.h"
41	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h"
42	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok15.h"
43	// SG2's elementwise tail is an Adam apply on the meta-net smart-grad; the
44	// metanet itself (supergrok2.h / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h) is the separate
45	// CSA/HCA launch. adamw.h already pulled in above covers the tail.
46	
47	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
48	
49	namespace algo = ::sg::algorithms;
50	
51	// Compile-time optimizer selector — one value per real optimizer (no aliases,
52	// no fallback). Must match grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py's set.
53	enum class OptId : int {
54	    AdamW = 0, Lion = 1, Grokfast = 2, GrokAdamW = 3, LookSAM = 4,
55	    Prodigy = 5, NeuralGrok = 6, Muon = 7, SuperGrok11 = 8,
56	    SuperGrok15 = 9, SuperGrok2 = 10
57	};
58	
59	// NeuralGrok / SG11 / SG15 psi/phi MLP hidden width (compile-time). Matches the
60	// per-op neuralgrok kernel's default instantiation.
61	static constexpr int kPsiHidden = 16;
62	
63	// #5 — NeuralGrok psi-net weight packing in the cell's `extra` buffer.
64	// neuralgrok has no per-element `extra` n-slice (its psi-net is a small
65	// per-TENSOR weight set), so the cell repurposes the otherwise-unused `extra`
66	// pointer to carry the packed psi-net weights in this fixed layout:
67	//   extra[0                  .. kPsiHidden)        = psi_W1  [kPsiHidden]
68	//   extra[kPsiHidden         .. 2*kPsiHidden)      = psi_b1  [kPsiHidden]
69	//   extra[2*kPsiHidden       .. 3*kPsiHidden)      = psi_W2  [kPsiHidden]
70	//   extra[3*kPsiHidden]                            = psi_b2  (scalar)
71	// A neuralgrok cell binds st.psi_W1/b1/W2 from these offsets so the device read
72	// of the psi weights is a real, bound pointer instead of a null-deref. psi_b2
73	// is a device scalar; the cell leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default (a host
74	// scalar cannot dereference a device pointer) — see the #5 stop in the report.
75	static constexpr int kPsiW1Off = 0;
76	static constexpr int kPsiB1Off = kPsiHidden;
77	static constexpr int kPsiW2Off = 2 * kPsiHidden;
78	static constexpr int kPsiB2Off = 3 * kPsiHidden;   // scalar slot (device-side)
79	static constexpr int kPsiPackFloats = 3 * kPsiHidden + 1;
80	
81	// All optimizer state any of the 11 tails may read. A given cell zero-fills the
82	// pointers its optimizer does not use; each apply_optimizer<> branch touches
83	// ONLY its own optimizer's real buffers (so unused ones are never dereferenced).
84	struct FusedOptState {
85	    // Adam-family moments (shared by almost all).
86	    float* exp_avg     = nullptr;   // m
87	    float* exp_avg_sq  = nullptr;   // v
88	    // Grokfast / GrokAdamW slow-gradient EMA.
89	    float* ema         = nullptr;
90	    // LookSAM precomputed SAM ascent direction.
91	    const float* sam_dir = nullptr;
92	    // Prodigy trajectory accumulator + adaptive d (scalar, host/reduce-stage).
93	    float* s_track     = nullptr;
94	    float  d_factor    = 1.0f;
95	    // SG11/SG15 momentum buffer + reduced cosine/accuracy gate (scalar).
96	    float* mu          = nullptr;
97	    float  gate        = 1.0f;
98	    // Muon precomputed Newton–Schulz orthogonalized direction + step scales.
99	    const float* orth  = nullptr;
100	    float  neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;
101	    float  decay_factor = 1.0f;
102	    // NeuralGrok psi-net (per-tensor MLP weights) — psi computed per element.
103	    const float* psi_W1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
104	    const float* psi_b1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
105	    const float* psi_W2 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
106	    float        psi_b2 = 0.0f;
107	    // SG2 smart-grad from the CSA/HCA meta-net launch (drives the Adam tail).
108	    const float* smart_grad = nullptr;
109	    // Shared hyperparameters.
110	    float lr = 1e-3f, beta1 = 0.9f, beta2 = 0.999f, eps = 1e-8f, wd = 0.01f;
111	    float bc1 = 1.0f, bc2 = 1.0f;       // un-inverted bias-corrections
112	    float alpha = 0.98f, beta = 0.0f, lamb = 2.0f, alpha_max = 1.0f;
113	};
114	
115	// =========================================================================
116	//  FusedScalars — the FULL runtime scalar set the host passes per fused_step.
117	//
118	//  C2-GAP FIX (the whole point of this struct). Previously each mega_*.cu host
119	//  entry bound ONLY pointers + lr into FusedOptState and left every other scalar
120	//  at its struct default — which silently froze the math: bc1/bc2 == 1.0 (NO
121	//  Adam bias correction, stuck at t=1), gate == 1.0 (SG gating inert), d_factor
122	//  == 1.0 (Prodigy d-adaptation inert), and beta1/beta2/eps/wd/alpha/lamb/
123	//  alpha_max/beta/neg_lr_scale/decay_factor never reaching apply_optimizer<>.
124	//  apply_optimizer<> already READS all of these from FusedOptState; the only gap
125	//  was that nobody SET them. This POD carries them across the host→kernel ABI so
126	//  the cell can populate FusedOptState with the live optimizer's real values.
127	//
128	//  Defaults here reproduce the OLD inert behavior EXACTLY (bc=gate=d_factor=1,
129	//  decay_factor=1, the same beta/eps/wd/alpha defaults), so a caller that does
130	//  not pass scalars yields byte-identical results to the pre-fix cells — the
131	//  widening is additive, not a behavior change for unset fields.
132	//
133	//  Per-tensor step count / bias correction (loud assumption): the megakernel
134	//  treats the whole flat param as ONE task, so a SINGLE (bc1, bc2) pair is bound
135	//  per call. That is correct ONLY when every parameter tensor shares the same
136	//  step counter — which holds in the grokking race (all params step together
137	//  every iteration). The host computes bc1 = 1 - beta1^step, bc2 = 1 - beta2^step
138	//  from that shared step and passes them here. If a future caller steps tensors
139	//  at different counts, it must call fused_step per-tensor with that tensor's bc.
140	// =========================================================================
141	struct FusedScalars {
142	    float lr           = 1e-3f;
143	    float beta1        = 0.9f;
144	    float beta2        = 0.999f;
145	    float eps          = 1e-8f;
146	    float wd           = 0.01f;
147	    float bc1          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta1^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
148	    float bc2          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta2^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
149	    float alpha        = 0.98f;  // meta-net strength / grokfast_alpha / neuralgrok alpha
150	    float beta         = 0.0f;   // neuralgrok beta (affine psi term)
151	    float lamb         = 2.0f;   // grokfast/grokadamw amplification (grokfast_lamb)
152	    float alpha_max    = 1.0f;   // SG15 per-coord alpha clip ceiling
153	    float gate         = 1.0f;   // SG11 cosine gate / SG15 sigmoid(accuracy) gate
154	    float d_factor     = 1.0f;   // Prodigy adaptive d (effective LR scale)
155	    float neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;   // Muon: -lr * ns_scale (2D NS-orth apply)
156	    float decay_factor = 1.0f;   // Muon: 1 - lr*wd (decoupled decay multiplier)
157	};
158	
159	// Fold the runtime scalars into a FusedOptState (pointers are bound separately
160	// by each cell). Single seam so every cell applies the SAME scalar mapping — no
161	// per-cell drift in which field a scalar lands in. apply_optimizer<> reads these
162	// exact fields, so this is the bridge that un-freezes bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor/etc.
163	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void apply_scalars(FusedOptState& st,
164	                                                        const FusedScalars& s) {
165	    st.lr           = s.lr;
166	    st.beta1        = s.beta1;
167	    st.beta2        = s.beta2;
168	    st.eps          = s.eps;
169	    st.wd           = s.wd;
170	    st.bc1          = s.bc1;
171	    st.bc2          = s.bc2;
172	    st.alpha        = s.alpha;
173	    st.beta         = s.beta;
174	    st.lamb         = s.lamb;
175	    st.alpha_max    = s.alpha_max;
176	    st.gate         = s.gate;
177	    st.d_factor     = s.d_factor;
178	    st.neg_lr_scale = s.neg_lr_scale;
179	    st.decay_factor = s.decay_factor;
180	}

182	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
183	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
184	template <OptId Opt>
185	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
186	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
187	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
188	    (void)step;
189	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
190	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
191	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
192	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
193	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
194	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
195	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
196	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
197	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
198	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
199	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
200	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
201	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
202	        algo::grokadamw_step<float, float>(
203	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
204	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
205	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
206	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
207	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
208	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
209	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
210	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
211	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
212	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
213	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
214	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
215	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
216	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
217	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
218	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
219	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
220	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
221	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
222	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
223	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
224	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
225	            fabsf(grad[idx]), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
226	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
227	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
228	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
229	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
230	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
231	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
232	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
233	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
234	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
235	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
236	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
237	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
238	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
239	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
240	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
241	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
242	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
243	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
244	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
245	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
246	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
247	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
248	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
249	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
250	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
251	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
252	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
253	    }
254	}

260	def make_data(p=97, frac_train=0.5, val_ratio=0.10, seed=42):
261	    rng = random.Random(seed)
262	    op_tok, eq_tok = p, p + 1
263	    pairs, labels = [], []
264	    for a in range(p):
265	        for b in range(1, p):
266	            b_inv = pow(b, p - 2, p)
267	            pairs.append([a, op_tok, b, eq_tok])
268	            labels.append((a * b_inv) % p)

270	    pairs, labels = zip(*c)

272	    n_val = int(n_train_total * val_ratio)

381	class ViT(nn.Module):
382	    def __init__(self, p=97, patch_dim=49, num_patches=16, d=128, h=4, nl=2, grad_checkpoint=True):
383	        super().__init__()
384	        self.patch_proj = nn.Linear(patch_dim, d)
385	        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, d) * 0.02)
386	        self.pos = nn.Embedding(num_patches + 1, d)
387	        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([EncoderBlock(d, h) for _ in range(nl)])
388	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, p)
389	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(num_patches + 1).unsqueeze(0))
390	        self.grad_checkpoint = grad_checkpoint
391	    def forward(self, x):
392	        B = x.size(0); h = self.patch_proj(x)
393	        h = torch.cat([self.cls_token.expand(B, -1, -1), h], dim=1)
394	        h = h + self.pos(self.pos_ids)
395	        for l in self.layers: h = _maybe_checkpoint(l, h, self.grad_checkpoint)
396	        return self.out(self.norm(h[:, 0, :]))

398	# ── Model 3: Mamba SSM ───────────────────────────────────────────────
399	class SelectiveSSMLayer(nn.Module):
400	    def __init__(self, d, state_dim=16, dt_rank=None, expand_factor=2):
401	        super().__init__()
402	        self.state_dim = state_dim; self.d_inner = d * expand_factor
403	        self.dt_rank = dt_rank or max(d // 16, 1)
404	        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d, self.d_inner * 2, bias=False)
405	        self.conv1d = nn.Conv1d(self.d_inner, self.d_inner, kernel_size=3,
406	                                padding=1, groups=self.d_inner, bias=True)
407	        self.x_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, self.dt_rank + state_dim * 2, bias=False)
408	        self.dt_proj = nn.Linear(self.dt_rank, self.d_inner, bias=True)
409	        A = torch.arange(1, state_dim + 1, dtype=torch.float32)
410	        self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A.unsqueeze(0).expand(self.d_inner, -1)))
411	        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.d_inner))
412	        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d, bias=False)
413	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d)
414	    def _selective_scan(self, x, dt, B, C):
415	        batch, L, _ = x.shape; A = -torch.exp(self.A_log); dt = F.softplus(dt)
416	        # Try CUDA kernel
417	        if x.is_cuda:
418	            try:
419	                from mamba_scan_ext import selective_scan_cuda
420	                return selective_scan_cuda(
421	                    x.contiguous(), dt.contiguous(),
422	                    B.contiguous(), C.contiguous(), A.contiguous()
423	                )
424	            except ImportError:
425	                pass
426	        # Python fallback
427	        h = torch.zeros(batch, self.d_inner, self.state_dim, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
428	        ys = []
429	        for t in range(L):
430	            dt_t = dt[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
431	            h = torch.exp(dt_t * A.unsqueeze(0)) * h + (dt_t * B[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)) * x[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
432	            ys.append((h * C[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)).sum(-1))
433	        return torch.stack(ys, dim=1)
434	    def forward(self, x):
435	        residual = x; xz = self.in_proj(x); x_main, z = xz.chunk(2, dim=-1)
436	        x_main = F.silu(self.conv1d(x_main.transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2))
437	        x_dbc = self.x_proj(x_main)

586	# scalars (lr/betas/eps/wd/bc1/bc2) and the persistent m|v state — all directly
587	# computable from the live optimizer + a step counter, with NO separate per-step
588	# precompute. The other 9 optimizers need a precomputed per-step quantity the L1
589	# tail reads but does not itself produce — prodigy's adaptive ``d``, grokfast/
590	# grokadamw's slow-grad EMA seeding, looksam's SAM direction, muon's NS-orth
591	# direction, SG11/15's reduced gate + mu, SG2's meta-net smart-grad. Those are
592	# honest-staged behind the readiness gate (a loud one-time TODO at run start)
593	# rather than wired with placeholder scalars (which would silently degrade the
594	# math — the exact suppression the owner forbids). ``register_fused`` is the seam
595	# to add them once their precompute is plumbed + validated.

597	# NOTE (L1 is model-agnostic): the L1 tail (fused_optimizer_stage<Opt>) never
598	# touches the model stages, so a cell's result depends only on the optimizer, not
599	# the model. All 3 models × {adamw, lion} are therefore equivalent on L1 and all
600	# are whitelisted; the parity test needs only ONE model per optimizer.
601	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

603	MODELS = ("transformer_decoder", "vit", "mamba3")
604	SHORT_MODELS = tuple(short_model_name(m) for m in MODELS)
605	OPTIMIZERS = ("adamw", "grokadamw", "grokfast", "lion", "looksam", "muon",
606	              "neuralgrok", "prodigy", "supergrok11", "supergrok15", "supergrok2")
607	OPT_CLASS = {
608	    "adamw":       "AdamW",
609	    "grokadamw":   "GrokAdamW",
610	    "grokfast":    "Grokfast",
611	    "lion":        "Lion",
612	    "looksam":     "LookSAM",
613	    "muon":        "Muon",
614	    "neuralgrok":  "NeuralGrok",
615	    "prodigy":     "Prodigy",
616	    "supergrok11": "SuperGrok11",
617	    "supergrok15": "SuperGrok15",
618	    "supergrok2":  "SuperGrok2",
619	}

621	# READINESS whitelist: (canonical_model, optimizer) cells cleared for the L1
622	# megakernel path this pass. Everything else uses the existing per-op/eager path.
623	# Kept as the SINGLE source of truth for "which cell may take the megakernel"; the
624	# validation script (tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py) asserts each of these
625	# matches its eager reference before it is trusted on hardware.
626	_FUSED_READY_OPTIMIZERS = ("adamw", "lion")
627	_FUSED_READY = frozenset(
628	    (m, o) for m in MODELS for o in _FUSED_READY_OPTIMIZERS
629	)
630	
631	_FUSED_REGISTRY = {}

634	def fused_ready_cells():
635	    """The (canonical_model, optimizer) pairs cleared for the L1 megakernel path.
636	
637	    Single source of truth for the readiness whitelist; the race and the
638	    validation script both read it so they cannot disagree on which cell is live.
639	    """
640	    return frozenset(_FUSED_READY)
641	
642	
643	def register_fused(model, optimizer, arch):
644	    """Register a fused (model, optimizer, arch) kernel callable.
645	
646	    Used to populate ``_FUSED_REGISTRY`` for the readiness-whitelisted cells (see
647	    ``_register_ready_cells`` below). The registered callable takes the same
648	    ``(params, inputs, grads, state, lr)`` shape ``dispatch_fused`` forwards.
649	    """
650	    def decorator(fn):
651	        _FUSED_REGISTRY[(canonicalize_model(model), optimizer, arch)] = fn
652	        return fn
653	    return decorator
654	
655	
656	def has_fused(model, optimizer, arch=None):
657	    """Whether the L1 megakernel path is available for (model, optimizer, arch).
658	
659	    True iff the cell is on the readiness whitelist (``_FUSED_READY``) for the
660	    detected arch. The arch must be a real GPU arch with a compiled fused TU
661	    (sm_90 / gfx942); on any other arch (CPU host, TPU) this returns False so the
662	    caller uses the eager path. Tolerant of an unknown model name (returns False).
663	    """
664	    if arch is None:
665	        try:
666	            arch = detect_arch()
667	        except UnsupportedArchError:
668	            return False
669	    try:
670	        model = canonicalize_model(model)
671	    except ValueError:
672	        return False
673	    # The compiled fused TU exists only for the GPU impl families (sm_90/gfx942).
674	    impl = normalize_arch(arch) if not isinstance(arch, int) else arch
675	    if impl not in (90, 942):
676	        return False
677	    return (model, optimizer) in _FUSED_READY
678	
679	
680	def dispatch_fused(model, optimizer, params, inputs, grads, state, lr, arch=None):
681	    """Dispatch to a registered fused kernel, or raise KeyError if none.
682	
683	    The whitelisted cells register a callable here via ``register_fused``; the
684	    race reaches the megakernel through the higher-level
685	    :func:`fused_optimizer_step` (which assembles persistent state + live
686	    scalars), so this remains the low-level registry shim.
687	    """
688	    if arch is None:
689	        arch = detect_arch()
690	    model = canonicalize_model(model)
691	    key = (model, optimizer, arch)
692	    if key not in _FUSED_REGISTRY:
693	        raise KeyError(
694	            f"No fused kernel for {key}. "
695	            f"Available: {list(_FUSED_REGISTRY.keys())}"
696	        )
697	    return _FUSED_REGISTRY[key](params, inputs, grads, state, lr)
698	
699	
700	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
701	# L1 megakernel optimizer-step driver (the live race path for whitelisted cells).
702	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
703	
704	# One-time run-start announcement guard (so the readiness summary prints ONCE per
705	# process, not per step — the owner directive: "says so ONCE loudly at run start").
706	_FUSED_ANNOUNCED = False
707	
708	
709	def announce_fused_readiness(force: bool = False) -> None:
710	    """Print, ONCE per process, which cells take the L1 megakernel path.
711	
712	    Loud + honest at run start: lists the whitelisted (model, optimizer) cells
713	    that will use the fused optimizer-tail megakernel and notes that every other
714	    cell uses the eager/per-op path. Idempotent (guarded by ``_FUSED_ANNOUNCED``).
715	    """
716	    global _FUSED_ANNOUNCED
717	    if _FUSED_ANNOUNCED and not force:
718	        return
719	    _FUSED_ANNOUNCED = True
720	    ready = sorted(f"{short_model_name(m)}:{o}" for (m, o) in _FUSED_READY)
721	    msg = (
722	        f"[fused] L1 megakernel path ENABLED for {len(ready)} cell(s): "
723	        f"{', '.join(ready)}. All other (model, optimizer) cells use the "
724	        f"eager/per-op path (L3 fwd+bwd+opt is a surrogate-model path, not "
725	        f"used by the race; see BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md).")
726	    # Print to stderr so the run-start banner is ALWAYS visible (the module
727	    # logger has a NullHandler by default, so logger.warning would be silent
728	    # unless GROK_LOG_LEVEL is set). Also log it for structured-log consumers.
729	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
730	    logger.warning(msg)
731	
732	
733	# Per-optimizer extra-state requirement for the L1 tail's `extra` (3rd n-slice).
734	# Only the whitelisted optimizers are listed; adamw/lion need no extra slice (it
735	# is allocated and zeroed but never read — rebase_state<Opt> guards it out).
736	_OPT_USES_EXTRA = {
737	    "adamw": False,
738	    "lion":  False,
739	}
740	
741	
742	def _opt_scalars_from(optimizer, step):
743	    """Extract the FULL scalar set for ``ops.fused_step`` from a live optimizer.
744	
745	    Pulls lr/betas/eps/weight_decay from ``param_groups[0]`` (so a scheduled lr is
746	    honored) and computes the UN-INVERTED bias corrections bc1 = 1 - beta1**step,
747	    bc2 = 1 - beta2**step from the shared step counter. One (bc1, bc2) pair is
748	    correct because the race steps every parameter together (the megakernel treats
749	    each flat param as one task; see opt_components.cuh FusedScalars note).
750	
751	    Returns a kwargs dict for ``ops.fused_step`` (only the fields the whitelisted
752	    optimizers consume are set; the rest keep their inert ABI defaults).
753	    """
754	    g = optimizer.param_groups[0]
755	    betas = g.get("betas", (0.9, 0.999))
756	    beta1, beta2 = float(betas[0]), float(betas[1])
757	    lr = float(g.get("lr", 1e-3))
758	    eps = float(g.get("eps", 1e-8))
759	    wd = float(g.get("weight_decay", 0.0))
760	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** step
761	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** step
762	    return dict(lr=lr, beta1=beta1, beta2=beta2, eps=eps, weight_decay=wd,
763	                bc1=bc1, bc2=bc2, step=int(step))
764	
765	
766	def fused_optimizer_step(model_name, opt_name, torch_module, optimizer, *,
767	                         state_cache, step):
768	    """Run ONE L1 fused optimizer-tail step over the live model's parameters.
769	
770	    This is the live race path for a readiness-whitelisted cell. The caller has
771	    ALREADY run the real forward + backward, so every trainable parameter carries
772	    its real ``p.grad``; this applies the canonical optimizer update to each
773	    parameter in-place via the fused megakernel (``ops.fused_step`` with
774	    ``opt_only=True`` → the L1 real-grad tail).
775	
776	    State ownership (critical): because the fused path REPLACES ``optimizer.step()``
777	    the torch optimizer's own ``.state`` never fills, so we keep our OWN persistent
778	    per-parameter ``[m|v|extra]`` (one contiguous 3n fp32 buffer) in
779	    ``state_cache`` (a dict the caller threads across steps). Reallocating it per
780	    step would reset momentum every step (the optimizer would never grok); we
781	    allocate once per parameter and reuse.
782	
783	    Args:
784	        model_name: user/canonical model name (canonicalized internally).
785	        opt_name: optimizer key (must be on the readiness whitelist).
786	        torch_module: the ``nn.Module`` being trained (provides named params+grads).
787	        optimizer: the live torch optimizer (source of lr/betas/eps/wd).
788	        state_cache: dict persisted across steps: id(param) -> 3n fp32 state tensor.
789	        step: 1-based step counter (drives bias correction).
790	
791	    Returns True on success. Raises if the cell is not whitelisted or a param is
792	    in an unsupported layout (no silent corruption).
793	    """
794	    model_c = canonicalize_model(model_name)
795	    if (model_c, opt_name) not in _FUSED_READY:
796	        raise KeyError(
797	            f"fused_optimizer_step: cell ({model_c}, {opt_name}) is not on the "
798	            f"L1 readiness whitelist {sorted(_FUSED_READY)}")
799	    ops = get_ops()
800	    if not hasattr(ops, "fused_step"):
801	        raise RuntimeError("ops.fused_step unavailable; build the extension.")
802	
803	    scalars = _opt_scalars_from(optimizer, step)
804	
805	    for _, p in torch_module.named_parameters():
806	        if not p.requires_grad:
807	            continue
808	        g = p.grad
809	        if g is None:
810	            # No grad for this param this step (e.g. an unused head). Skip it
811	            # rather than feed a stale/zero buffer — the eager step would also be
812	            # a no-op for a None grad.
813	            continue
814	        # The L1 tail indexes raw dense float memory; a non-contiguous param/grad
815	        # or a non-fp32 dtype would silently address the wrong elements. fused_step
816	        # does NOT run check_param_grad (that guard is on the per-op path), so we
817	        # enforce it here. amp is off by default in the race (fp32 params).
818	        if p.dtype != torch.float32 or g.dtype != torch.float32:
819	            raise RuntimeError(
820	                f"fused_optimizer_step requires fp32 params AND grads (got "
821	                f"param {p.dtype}, grad {g.dtype}); the L1 megakernel tail reads "
822	                f"raw float memory. Disable AMP for the fused path.")
823	        if g.is_sparse:
824	            raise RuntimeError("fused_optimizer_step does not support sparse grads")
825	        param = p.data if p.data.is_contiguous() else p.data.contiguous()
826	        grad = g if g.is_contiguous() else g.contiguous()
827	        n = param.numel()
828	        key = id(p)
829	        st = state_cache.get(key)
830	        if st is None or st.numel() != 3 * n:
831	            # Persistent [m|v|extra] state, zero-init ONCE per parameter.
832	            st = torch.zeros(3 * n, dtype=torch.float32, device=param.device)
833	            state_cache[key] = st
834	        # input is unused on the L1 tail (auto in = input.numel()? : p); pass the
835	        # param as a harmless non-empty placeholder so the C++ side does not fall
836	        # back to the acts buffer. grad is the REAL gradient just computed.
837	        ops.fused_step(model_c, opt_name, param.view(-1), param.view(-1),
838	                       grad.view(-1), st, scalars["lr"],
839	                       beta1=scalars["beta1"], beta2=scalars["beta2"],
840	                       eps=scalars["eps"], weight_decay=scalars["weight_decay"],
841	                       bc1=scalars["bc1"], bc2=scalars["bc2"],
842	                       step=scalars["step"], opt_only=True)
843	        # If .contiguous() copied, write the update back into the param storage.
844	        if param.data_ptr() != p.data.data_ptr():
845	            p.data.copy_(param.view_as(p.data))
846	    return True
847	
848	
849	def _register_ready_cells():
850	    """Populate ``_FUSED_REGISTRY`` for every readiness-whitelisted cell.
851	
852	    The registered callable is a thin shim so ``dispatch_fused`` / ``has_fused``
853	    see a real entry; the live race uses :func:`fused_optimizer_step` directly
854	    (it owns the persistent state + per-step scalars the low-level registry shim
855	    cannot carry). Registering for the detected GPU arch only (the compiled TU).
856	    """
857	    try:
858	        arch = detect_arch()
859	    except UnsupportedArchError:
860	        return
861	    impl = normalize_arch(arch) if not isinstance(arch, int) else arch
862	    if impl not in (90, 942):
863	        return
864	    for (m, o) in _FUSED_READY:
865	        def _shim(params, inputs, grads, state, lr, _m=m, _o=o):
866	            ops = get_ops()
867	            ops.fused_step(_m, _o, params, inputs, grads, state, float(lr),
868	                           opt_only=True)
869	            return params
870	        register_fused(m, o, arch)(_shim)
871	
872	
873	# Populate the registry at import (no-op / silent on CPU + non-GPU arches).
874	_register_ready_cells()

2	// dispatch.cpp — single-source arch detection + fused_step dispatch
3	//
4	// Arch-honest LOUD-GATE dispatch (Phase 8). The kernel source has real bodies
5	// only for sm_90/sm_90a (one CUDA tree, sg::sm90) and gfx942 (one HIP tree,
6	// sg::gfx942). detect_arch_from_device() therefore returns 90 for NVIDIA

8	// sm_80, which has no TMA/WGMMA path) rather than silently running Hopper SASS
9	// on the wrong architecture. FORCE_ARCH is the explicit operator override.
10	// TPU arch is handled in Python via JAX.

34	int detect_arch_from_env() {
35	 const char* force = std::getenv("FORCE_ARCH");
36	 if (!force) return -1;
37	 std::string s(force);
38	 // TPU is handled in Python; not valid for C++ dispatch.
39	 if (s.rfind("tpu", 0) == 0) {
40	 throw std::runtime_error(
41	 "FORCE_ARCH=" + s + " is not a GPU arch; TPU dispatch is handled "
42	 "in Python via JAX.");
43	 }
44	 // AMD: any gfx target (and the bare 942 form) -> the gfx942 impl.
45	 if (s == "942" || s.rfind("gfx", 0) == 0) return 942;
46	 // NVIDIA: any sm_* / smXX form -> the sm90 impl.
47	 if (s.rfind("sm_", 0) == 0 || s.rfind("sm", 0) == 0) return 90;
48	 // Bare numeric compute capability (e.g. "70", "90", "120") -> NVIDIA.
49	 if (!s.empty() && s.find_first_not_of("0123456789") == std::string::npos)
50	 return 90;
51	 throw std::runtime_error(
52	 "FORCE_ARCH=" + s +
53	 " not recognized. Use an NVIDIA arch (sm_70..sm_120 or a numeric "
54	 "compute capability), an AMD arch (gfx906..gfx1201), or run TPU via "
55	 "Python/JAX.");

63	 throw std::runtime_error(
64	 std::string("cudaGetDevice failed: ") + cudaGetErrorString(err));

67	 // reads) instead of the full cudaGetDeviceProperties struct copy.

72	 std::string("cudaDeviceGetAttribute(ComputeCapabilityMajor) failed: ") +
73	 cudaGetErrorString(err));

78	 std::string("cudaDeviceGetAttribute(ComputeCapabilityMinor) failed: ") +

132	 "has only the gfx942 (CDNA3 / MI300X) body. Supported: sm_90a "

250	// Phase 2: expanded to cover all 99 cells (3 models × 11 optimizers × 3 archs).

260	// Per-(device, n) reusable scratch for fused_step. The barrier counters and the
261	// `acts` proxy were previously reallocated (and `acts` memset over the full
262	// param size) on EVERY dispatch; sizes/offsets are constant for a given n.
263	// We persist them keyed by (device_index, n) and only reset the mutable parts
264	// (zero the 3 barrier counters + the acts buffer) per step. Behavior is
265	// identical — same zero-initialized scratch handed to the launcher — but the
266	// allocations/the full-size memset of sizes/offsets happen once per shape.
267	struct FusedScratch {
268	 torch::Tensor g_next;       // int32 [1]
269	 torch::Tensor g_arrived;    // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
270	 torch::Tensor g_generation; // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
271	 torch::Tensor sizes;        // int32 [1] = n  (constant per n)
272	 torch::Tensor offsets;      // int32 [1] = 0  (constant)
273	 torch::Tensor acts;         // float [numel(params)] proxy buffer
274	};
275	
276	// Keyed by (device_index, n). n disambiguates differing param shapes on the
277	// same device; acts is sized to params.numel() (== n here, single flat tensor).
278	inline FusedScratch& fused_scratch_for(const torch::Tensor& params, int64_t n) {
279	 static std::unordered_map<long long, FusedScratch> cache;
280	 const long long dev_idx =
281	 params.device().is_cuda() ? static_cast<long long>(params.device().index())
282	 : -1LL;
283	 const long long key = (dev_idx << 40) ^ static_cast<long long>(n);
284	 auto it = cache.find(key);
285	 if (it == cache.end()) {
286	 auto opts_i =
287	 torch::TensorOptions().device(params.device()).dtype(torch::kInt32);
288	 FusedScratch s;
289	 s.g_next = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
290	 s.g_arrived = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
291	 s.g_generation = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
292	 s.sizes = torch::full({1}, n, opts_i); // constant for this n
293	 s.offsets = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i); // constant
294	 s.acts = torch::zeros_like(params);
295	 it = cache.emplace(key, std::move(s)).first;
296	 } else {
297	 // Reset only the mutable scratch; sizes/offsets are invariant for this n.
298	 it->second.g_next.zero_();
299	 it->second.g_arrived.zero_();
300	 it->second.g_generation.zero_();
301	 it->second.acts.zero_();
302	 }
303	 return it->second;
304	}
305	#endif

307	} // anonymous namespace

309	// NOTE: the default argument VALUES live on the declaration in helpers.h (which
310	// bindings.cpp sees for the py::arg defaults). C++ forbids repeating a default
311	// argument on both the declaration and the definition, so the definition below
312	// lists the parameters WITHOUT defaults. Keep the two signatures in lock-step:
313	// (model, optimizer, params, input, grad, state, lr, beta1, beta2, eps,
314	//  weight_decay, alpha, lamb, gamma, gate, d_factor, bc1, bc2, neg_lr_scale,
315	//  decay_factor, beta, alpha_max, step, opt_only).
316	void fused_step(const std::string& model, const std::string& optimizer,
317	 torch::Tensor params, torch::Tensor input,
318	 torch::Tensor grad, torch::Tensor state, float lr,
319	 // FULL scalar set (C2-gap fix). apply_optimizer<> reads every one of
320	 // these; before this widening only `lr` was bound and the rest sat at
321	 // FusedOptState defaults (bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor == 1.0 → NO bias
322	 // correction, SG gating + Prodigy d-adaptation inert). bc1/bc2 are
323	 // un-inverted (= 1 - beta^step); the caller computes them from the shared
324	 // step counter (valid because all race params step together — the
325	 // megakernel treats the flat param as one task with one bc pair).
326	 float beta1, float beta2, float eps,
327	 float weight_decay, float alpha, float lamb,
328	 float gamma, float gate, float d_factor,
329	 float bc1, float bc2,
330	 float neg_lr_scale, float decay_factor,
331	 float beta, float alpha_max,
332	 int64_t step,
333	 // Tier selector. opt_only=true → L1: fused optimizer TAIL only; the kernel
334	 // reads the REAL grad from `grad` (framework-computed) and applies the
335	 // canonical update — the numerically-faithful path the race uses.
336	 // opt_only=false → L3: the kernel also runs the SURROGATE element-local
337	 // model fwd/bwd (model_stages.*), whose loss does NOT match the real
338	 // Transformer/ViT/Mamba graph (see BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md).
339	 bool opt_only) {
340	 int arch = detect_arch();
341	 std::string arch_str = (arch == 90) ? "sm_90"
342	 : (arch == 942) ? "gfx942" : "tpu_v6e";
343	 // `gamma` is carried for ABI completeness / forward-compat (the directive's
344	 // scalar set lists it). No current apply_optimizer<> branch consumes a gamma
345	 // term — SG15's gamma_alpha folds into the host-side alpha schedule (it
346	 // arrives here already baked into `alpha`), so binding it again would double-
347	 // apply. Kept in the ABI so a future cell can read it without re-widening.
348	 (void)gamma;
349	
350	 const std::string cell = wired_fused_cell(model, optimizer, arch);
351	 if (cell.empty()) {
352	 // §1.12 fall-through: no fused TU for this cell. The caller uses the
353	 // existing per-op dispatch (the per-optimizer *_fused_step bindings),
354	 // which is untouched. We surface a clear, non-silent signal.
355	 throw std::runtime_error(
356	 "no fused TU for (" + model + ", " + optimizer + ", " + arch_str +
357	 "); use the per-op path. Wired L3 cells: (mamba3,adamw), "
358	 "(transformer_decoder,lion), (vit,supergrok15).");
359	 }
360	
361	#if defined(WITH_CUDA) && !defined(WITH_HIP)
362	 if (arch == 90) {
363	 // Prepare the megakernel inputs from the tensors. The persistent scratch
364	 // (task counter + barrier state) is device-allocated and zero-initialized
365	 // here; the host launcher pins one CTA per SM. `state` carries the
366	 // optimizer state slices (m, v) concatenated; sizes/offsets describe the
367	 // per-parameter-tensor layout (here the single flattened tensor).
368	 //
369	 // Keep the element count in int64 at this boundary: a large flat param
370	 // ( > 2^31-1 elements ) truncated to `int` would wrap negative, making
371	 // the `3*n` state-size check pass spuriously and the `m + n` / `m + 2*n`
372	 // pointer offsets index out of bounds (silent OOB corruption). The
373	 // numel-derived state check and pointer math below all use this int64 n.
374	 const int64_t n = params.numel();
375	
376	 // Reusable per-(device,n) scratch: counters/acts reset, sizes/offsets fixed.
377	 FusedScratch& sc = fused_scratch_for(params, n);
378	
379	 // acts proxy + the m/v halves of state.
380	 auto p = params.data_ptr<float>();
381	 auto in = input.numel() ? input.data_ptr<float>() : p;
382	 auto gr = grad.numel() ? grad.data_ptr<float>() : sc.acts.data_ptr<float>();
383	 // state holds [m | v | extra]; split it. `extra` is the per-optimizer third
384	 // per-element buffer (ema/sam_dir/s_track/mu/orth/smart_grad); each cell binds
385	 // it to its FusedOptState field (adamw/lion/neuralgrok ignore it). Sized 3n.
386	 // An undersized state tensor was previously silently replaced by a fresh
387	 // zero buffer that was DISCARDED after the call (the optimizer state never
388	 // persisted) and reallocated every step — a latent correctness bug plus a
389	 // hot-path realloc. Surface it instead of silently corrupting state.
390	 if (state.numel() < 3 * n) {
391	 throw std::runtime_error(
392	 "fused_step: state tensor for (" + model + ", " + optimizer +
393	 ") has " + std::to_string(state.numel()) + " elements but needs at "
394	 "least 3*n = " + std::to_string(3 * n) +
395	 " (m|v|extra). Pass a persistent, correctly-sized state tensor.");
396	 }
397	 float* m = state.data_ptr<float>();
398	 float* v = m + n;
399	 float* extra = m + 2 * n;
400	
401	 // The megakernel ABI (PersistentContext.n_tasks, the int32 sizes/offsets
402	 // tensors) is 32-bit per the layout-identical mirror struct and the
403	 // generated launchers. The fused indices are being widened by the fused
404	 // agent; until the device-side N is int64, fail loudly rather than feed a
405	 // truncated count into the kernel (which would silently process the wrong
406	 // task range). This gate fires only for params with > 2^31-1 elements.
407	 TORCH_CHECK(n <= static_cast<int64_t>(std::numeric_limits<int>::max()),
408	 "fused_step: param has ", n, " elements, exceeding the int32 "
409	 "megakernel ABI (PersistentContext.n_tasks / sizes / offsets). "
410	 "Use the per-op path for params with > 2^31-1 elements.");
411	
412	 fused::PersistentContext ctx{
413	 sc.g_next.data_ptr<int>(),
414	 reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(sc.g_arrived.data_ptr<int>()),
415	 reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(sc.g_generation.data_ptr<int>()),
416	 // n_tasks = number of work tasks = #entries in sizes/offsets (one slab per
417	 // parameter tensor; a single flat tensor here → 1). It is NOT the element
418	 // count: the megakernel loops `t < n_tasks` reading sizes[t]/offsets[t], so
419	 // n_tasks=n would index both 1-element arrays ~n entries out of bounds and
420	 // feed garbage offsets into params[] (a multi-GB OOB read). n_ctas (0 here)
421	 // is overwritten by the launcher with one persistent CTA per SM.
422	 static_cast<int>(sc.sizes.numel()), 0u};
423	
424	 // Use the current CUDA stream so the megakernel orders against the rest of
425	 // the model's work and is capturable in a CUDA graph (the legacy default
426	 // stream 0 serialized against all work and blocked graph capture).
427	 cudaStream_t stream = c10::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream().stream();
428	
429	 // Pack the FULL scalar set for this cell. apply_optimizer<> reads every one
430	 // (the C2-gap fix); the cell's apply_scalars() copies them into FusedOptState.
431	 // Field order MUST match fused::sm90::FusedScalars (lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd,
432	 // bc1, bc2, alpha, beta, lamb, alpha_max, gate, d_factor, neg_lr_scale,
433	 // decay_factor). bc1/bc2 are un-inverted (= 1 - beta^step) — ONE pair per call
434	 // is correct because the megakernel processes the flat param as a single task
435	 // and all race params share `step`.
436	 fused::sm90::FusedScalars scalars{
437	 lr, beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay, bc1, bc2, alpha, beta, lamb,
438	 alpha_max, gate, d_factor, neg_lr_scale, decay_factor};
439	
440	 // Route to the real composed cell launcher (all 33 sm_90 cells). `found`
441	 // is set false only if no cell matches (then we fall through to the honest
442	 // not-compiled signal below). `opt_only` selects L1 (faithful real-grad tail)
443	 // vs L3 (surrogate-model fwd+bwd+opt).
444	 bool found = false;
445	 cudaError_t err = fused::sm90::dispatch_sm90_cell(
446	 model, optimizer, ctx, p, in, sc.acts.data_ptr<float>(), gr, m, v, extra,
447	 sc.sizes.data_ptr<int>(), sc.offsets.data_ptr<int>(), lr,
448	 static_cast<int>(step), scalars, opt_only, stream, &found);
449	
450	 if (found) {
451	 if (err != cudaSuccess)
452	 throw std::runtime_error(
453	 std::string("fused megakernel launch failed for ") + cell + ": " +
454	 cudaGetErrorString(err));
455	 return;
456	 }
457	 }
458	#endif
459	
460	#if defined(WITH_HIP)
461	 if (arch == 942) {
462	 // gfx942 real composition route (hipcc/MI300X). Mirror of the sm_90 path.
463	 // int64 element count at the boundary (see the sm_90 path for rationale):
464	 // a truncated `int` numel would wrap negative and make the 3*n check and
465	 // m+n/m+2*n pointer math index out of bounds.
466	 const int64_t n = params.numel();
467	 FusedScratch& sc = fused_scratch_for(params, n);
468	 auto p = params.data_ptr<float>();
469	 auto in = input.numel() ? input.data_ptr<float>() : p;
470	 auto gr = grad.numel() ? grad.data_ptr<float>() : sc.acts.data_ptr<float>();
471	 if (state.numel() < 3 * n) {
472	 throw std::runtime_error(
473	 "fused_step: state tensor for (" + model + ", " + optimizer +
474	 ") has " + std::to_string(state.numel()) + " elements but needs at "
475	 "least 3*n = " + std::to_string(3 * n) +
476	 " (m|v|extra). Pass a persistent, correctly-sized state tensor.");
477	 }
478	 float* m = state.data_ptr<float>();
479	 float* v = m + n; float* extra = m + 2 * n;
480	 // int32 megakernel ABI gate (mirror of the sm_90 path).
481	 TORCH_CHECK(n <= static_cast<int64_t>(std::numeric_limits<int>::max()),
482	 "fused_step: param has ", n, " elements, exceeding the int32 "
483	 "megakernel ABI. Use the per-op path for > 2^31-1 elements.");
484	 fused::gfx942_mega::PersistentContext ctx{
485	 sc.g_next.data_ptr<int>(),
486	 reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(sc.g_arrived.data_ptr<int>()),
487	 reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(sc.g_generation.data_ptr<int>()),
488	 // n_tasks = TASK count (sizes/offsets entries), NOT the element count n —
489	 // the megakernel loops t < n_tasks reading sizes[t]/offsets[t]; passing n
490	 // here was the same multi-GB OOB the sm_90 path fixed (47d8007), left
491	 // unfixed on this HIP twin until now.
492	 static_cast<int>(sc.sizes.numel()), 0u};
493	 // Current HIP stream for graph capture / proper ordering (was default 0).
494	 hipStream_t stream = c10::hip::getCurrentHIPStream().stream();
495	 // FULL scalar set (mirror of the sm_90 path); field order matches
496	 // fused::gfx942_mega::FusedScalars. bc1/bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^step).
497	 fused::gfx942_mega::FusedScalars scalars{
498	 lr, beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay, bc1, bc2, alpha, beta, lamb,
499	 alpha_max, gate, d_factor, neg_lr_scale, decay_factor};
500	 bool found = false;
501	 hipError_t herr = fused::gfx942_mega::dispatch_gfx942_cell(
502	 model, optimizer, ctx, p, in, sc.acts.data_ptr<float>(), gr, m, v, extra,
503	 sc.sizes.data_ptr<int>(), sc.offsets.data_ptr<int>(), lr,
504	 static_cast<int>(step), scalars, opt_only, stream, &found);
505	 if (found) {
506	 if (herr != hipSuccess)
507	 throw std::runtime_error(
508	 std::string("gfx942 fused megakernel launch failed for ") + cell +
509	 ": " + hipGetErrorString(herr));
510	 return;
511	 }
512	 }
513	#endif
514	
515	 // The cell is "wired" in the manifest but its TU is not compiled into THIS
516	 // build (CPU/host build has no fused TU). Surface it honestly.
517	 throw std::runtime_error(
518	 "fused TU for " + cell + " is manifest-registered but not compiled into "
519	 "this build (CPU build has no fused TU). Use the per-op path.");
520	}
521	
522	} // namespace sg

3	Given the feasibility solver (``megakernel.solve_all`` / ``megakernel.solve``),
4	this module EMITS the per-(model × optimizer × arch) megakernel source by
5	instantiating the ONE templated L3 megakernel from
6	``csrc/fused/<arch>/megakernel_demo.{cu,hip.hpp}`` at the solver-chosen tier.

8	You do NOT hand-write 99 kernels: the demo TU is the structural template, and
9	the generator re-instantiates ``l3_megakernel<Model, Optimizer>`` (sm_90 /
10	gfx942) or emits the Pallas program (tpu_v6e) per cell. It can emit a single
11	cell's source string (``--emit <model> <optimizer> <arch>``) or report the full
12	99-cell manifest with tiers (``--emit-all``).
13	
14	The set of cells that already have a REAL, wired fused TU (the three the demo
15	instantiates + dispatch.cpp routes to) is :data:`WIRED_CELLS`; every other cell
16	is generator-emittable but not yet compiled into the extension (the manifest
17	flags which is which, mirroring dispatch.cpp's honesty contract, §1.12).
18	
19	BUILD-TIME GENERATOR — NOT a runtime module. It is invoked from the build
20	(``setup.py`` materializes the per-cell sources it emits) and as a CLI::

24	    python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen --write-all

93	# Per-optimizer "extra" state buffer (a single n-element slice beyond m, v) that
94	# the fused tail reads. The host passes `extra` = state + 2n; each cell binds it
95	# to its optimizer's FusedOptState field. None → optimizer needs no third
96	# per-element buffer (adamw/lion). neuralgrok is special: its psi-net is a small
97	# per-tensor weight set (not an n-slice), so it stays host-supplied (🟡) and is
98	# NOT bound from `extra`.
99	_OPT_EXTRA_FIELD: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {
100	    "adamw": None,
101	    "lion": None,
102	    "grokfast": "ema",
103	    "grokadamw": "ema",
104	    "looksam": "sam_dir",
105	    "prodigy": "s_track",
106	    "neuralgrok": None,        # psi-net weights bound explicitly — see below
107	    "muon": "orth",
108	    "supergrok11": "mu",
109	    "supergrok15": "mu",
110	    "supergrok2": "smart_grad",
111	}

113	# NeuralGrok needs its psi-net weights bound from the packed `extra` buffer
114	# (layout W1|b1|W2|b2 in opt_components.{cuh,hip.hpp}). It does NOT use a single
115	# `extra` n-slice field like the other optimizers, so it gets a bespoke bind
116	# block instead of the generic `st.<field> = extra` / `(void)extra` line. The
117	# psi_b2 scalar is left host-side at 0 and read ON-DEVICE (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden],
118	# where the device pointer is dereferenceable). This keeps the codegen the
119	# single source for the cells (the bind used to be hand-patched into the files).
120	_PSI_BIND_CUDA = """
121	    // #5: bind the psi-net weights from the packed `extra` buffer (layout in
122	    // opt_components.cuh: W1|b1|W2|b2). Without this the psi pointers stay null
123	    // and neuralgrok_psi_forward null-derefs on this real path.
124	    if (extra) {
125	        st.psi_W1 = extra + kPsiW1Off;
126	        st.psi_b1 = extra + kPsiB1Off;
127	        st.psi_W2 = extra + kPsiW2Off;
128	        // st.psi_b2 left at 0.0f host-side: the real psi_b2 scalar lives at
129	        // extra[kPsiB2Off] and is read ON-DEVICE in apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok>
130	        // (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]), where the device pointer is dereferenceable.
131	    }"""
132	
133	_PSI_BIND_HIP = """
134	    // #5: bind psi-net weights from the packed `extra` buffer (W1|b1|W2|b2,
135	    // layout in opt_components.hip.hpp) — without this the psi pointers are null
136	    // and sg_psi_forward null-derefs. psi_b2 is read on-device in apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
137	    if (extra) {
138	        st.psi_W1 = extra + kPsiW1Off;
139	        st.psi_b1 = extra + kPsiB1Off;
140	        st.psi_W2 = extra + kPsiW2Off;
141	    }"""
